NEGATIVE.description: A response that redirects distress toward another person through hostility, blame, contempt, or dismissal.
NEGATIVE.visualBodyLanguage: posture tightens, gestures become sharp, and conversational distance feels confrontational

POSITIVE.description: A response that acknowledges emotion without passing harm to the other person.
POSITIVE.visualBodyLanguage: breathing slows, hands open, and posture becomes more balanced

UNCLEAR.description: The spoken response cannot be classified with sufficient confidence.
UNCLEAR.visualBodyLanguage: the scene holds without changing emotional state

voiceInterpretationContract.belowThresholdBehavior: ask the player to respond again
voiceInterpretationContract.prohibitedBehavior: do not change Monster state from an UNCLEAR response

transitions.designAssumption: A negative response after one positive response restores the host's Monster to FULL and propagates a new Monster.

emotionalContinuityRules: Emotion classification changes engine state before any visual prompt is generated.
Visko portrays the approved visible consequence but does not decide the category.
A negative response never removes the original host's Monster.
Two consecutive positive responses are required to remove a FULL Monster.
An unclear response produces no Monster change and no global count change.
